conventions.convention: R_k averages an integrable, jointly measurable real-valued loss over k IID training observations and an independent test observation. Training tuples follow increasing index order.

Splits have disjoint nonempty training and validation sets covering [n]. Schedule weights are nonnegative and sum to one; randomized schedules must be independent of observations. K-fold weights are fold size divided by n.

The covariance decomposition assumes a fixed balanced partition n=Km, symmetric learning rules, and square-integrable errors or paired differences. When m=1, the unused within-fold covariance is defined as zero.

A universal variance estimator may use the full sample, known rule, loss, and split, but cannot depend on the unknown law. Auxiliary randomization has a fixed law independent of the sample and unknown law.
Model consistency is label-specific convergence of the probability of selecting the specified true label to one. Candidate labels need not have distinct observation laws.

load_bearing.statement: The risk at training size k is R_k := E[L(A_k(Z_1,…,Z_k),Z_{k+1})] under P^(k+1), with an independent test observation. The fixed-partition target is Σ_j (|I_j|/n)R_{n−|I_j|}.
For an admissible finite weighted split schedule, output Σ_r (w_r/|V_r|)Σ_{i∈V_r} L(A_|T_r|(z_T_r),z_i). Paired comparison uses the same schedule and averages validation-loss differences.

For IID observations and a fixed admissible finite schedule with the stated measurability and integrability assumptions, E[R̂]=Σ_r w_r R_|T_r|. Its bias for R_n is Σ_r w_r(R_|T_r|−R_n). Independent finite-range schedule randomization averages the conditional identities.
Under its fixed balanced-fold, IID, symmetry, and second-moment hypotheses, Var(n⁻¹Σ_i e_i)=σ²/n+(m−1)ω/n+(n−m)γ/n, including paired loss differences.

For every fixed balanced K-fold design, no sample-based procedure independent of the unknown law is unbiased for the score variance for every IID law and every symmetric learning rule with measurable loss and finite score variance. The explicit fixed product rule already prevents unbiasedness over all Bernoulli(p), 0<p<1.
